pr_title: Add support for processing Unified TLS frames
pr_body:
This is mix of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/68425, https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/pull/1656 and reaction to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/64322.

Unified parsing works only on Windows as legacy and allows (old) clients to send TLS frame encoded in Ssl2 format.
All we really need is to process first frame. Server should respond back with "normal" TLS e.g. all the framing and processing removed in #64322 is really not needed. 

Since the header size is now variable, I changed `TlsFrameHelper` to return length of the TLS frame instead of just length of the inner payload.

Since we don't have good way how to generate real traffic, I added test that injects legacy ClientHello and verifies that we get back ServerHello instead of failure.  

fixes #68310

issue_context.title: CertificateSelection callback is not called when client use Unified framing
issue_context.body:
Some older TLS implementations can use Unified framing e.g. legacy SSL2 format with TLS 1.x body. 
With 6.0, we fail to detect the client hello and therefore we fail to call the callback.
This is going to fail completely with 7.0 code base.

Triage: Used by YARP customer with older devices.

Just to elaborate little bit more:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14356188/164564055-e3c8e45a-4157-4d2b-bd11-3eabcc9ebb4d.png)

The example above is TLS 1.0 session. The first frame comes in as sslv2/Unified formatted hello and server respond with "normal" TLS 1.0 ServerHello. This generally prevents any TLS extensions but it would achieve TLS 1.0 security e.g. no real ssl2 involvement.

review_comments: Shouldn't the two branches be swapped?

The naming may not be clear but if `useOptionCallback` is `true` we use `AuthenticateAsServerAsync(ServerOptionsSelectionCallback, Object, CancellationToken)` and `AuthenticateAsServerAsync(SslServerAuthenticationOptions, CancellationToken)` in opposite case. 

So there is callback in either branch but we either return whole options or just the certificate. 
Former depends on detecting ClinetHello so it is different code path.
